prompt: With an ephemeral exchange, what does the server's long-term key still do?

choices.text: It encrypts every record of the session
It signs, to prove who the server is
It is mixed into the shared secret so it can be recovered later
Nothing: it is no longer needed

prompt: Which of these give forward secrecy? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Any TLS 1.3 connection
choices.why: Yes: only ephemeral exchanges exist in it.

choices.text: A TLS 1.2 suite whose name starts TLS_ECDHE_
A TLS 1.2 suite using RSA key transport
choices.why: No: the server key unwraps every session.

choices.text: An SSH connection
choices.why: Yes: SSH runs an ephemeral exchange for each one.

choices.text: Because X25519 keys are too short
Because the attacker uses the same secret as Ana
